subject: Clarify: what stays in logs by default (streaming tokens, KV cache, prompts/outputs)
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@brightbank.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on what you persist by default (streamed tokens, KV cache, prompts)

Sean —

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our security team as we map Redwood into our data flow. We're trying to understand the "default" behavior without any special configuration. Specific questions: 

1) For streaming responses, do you persist partial tokens (the fragments we see streamed to the client) or only the final assembled response?
2) Is the serving KV cache (used to speed up repeated context) ever written to disk or retained in logs/audit stores?
3) How do you categorize: raw user prompt, model-generated intermediate tokens (if any), final model output — which of these are kept by default and for how long?
4) Any examples of edge cases that *do* cause persistence (e.g., function calls, attachments, or reranked results)?

We're preparing a short control mapping for SOC2 and would appreciate a brief example or matrix of what is kept by default and what customers can opt out of.

—Sam
Sam Patel
Information Security
BrightBank

From: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@brightbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on what you persist by default (streamed tokens, KV cache, prompts)

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kim (security/compliance), Marissa (product) and Karthik (infra) who can give detail. High level answers below; Kim will follow with a short matrix and one-pager we can attach to your SOC2 map.

Quick answers (high-level):
- Streaming: partial tokens are transient in-memory during the session. We persist the final response if the customer is on Hosted API with default capture enabled; partial streamed fragments are not stored as separate records.
- KV cache: runtime-only, not written to customer-facing logs or audit buckets by default.
- Classification: by default we persist the request (user prompt) and the final model output for 30 days (customer can change). Derivatives (embeddings, reranks) are controlled separately.

Kim — can you attach the retention matrix and call out the handful of edge cases Sam asked about (attachments, function/tool call payloads, reranked results)?

Sean
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@brightbank.com>, sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on what you persist by default (streamed tokens, KV cache, prompts)

Hi Sam — thanks for raising these. Below is a concise matrix and a few clarifying examples. I'm attaching a downloadable matrix (retention_matrix_v2.xlsx) and linking our public doc for full policy language. If you'd like, we can convert the matrix into a short statement you can include in your SOC2 evidence folder.

Retention matrix (default hosted API behavior, unless customer opts-in/opts-out or has Dedicated/Private deployment controls):
- User request (raw prompt + metadata): persisted by default, retained for 30 days (purge schedule: daily tombstone marking, 7-day purge job after tombstone).
- Final model output: persisted by default, retained for 30 days (same purge flow).
- Streaming fragments (partial tokens): not persisted as independent records. They exist transiently in memory while the request is being served; only the final assembled output is written to the request/response record when capture is enabled.
- KV cache / runtime caches: ephemeral in-memory caches tied to the serving instance. Not written to logs, not stored in object storage by default. When a customer uses Dedicated or Private with a custom persistence config, customers can elect to snapshot caches for debugging — that is non-default and requires explicit consenting configuration and access controls.
- Function/tool call payloads (the "tool result" that the model receives or returns): treated as part of the request/response record if capture is enabled; attachments referenced in tool results are stored as attachment stubs and appear in the retention matrix as files (we record filename, mime-type, and timestamp — we do not inline binary content in platform logs).
- Embeddings/reranks/derived artifacts: these are treated as derived artifacts. By default, embeddings are not persisted in the same retention bucket unless a customer calls the embeddings API where persistence rules differ (we surface that at time of call). Reranked candidate lists generated as part of a single request are persisted as part of the final response when capture is enabled.

Edge cases and examples:
- If a streaming session is interrupted mid-request (client disconnect), we will not have a final response to persist; by default nothing is written. However, we do retain a short-lived request metadata record to help with debugging (TTL of 24 hours) which contains non-user-content telemetry about the session (not the token stream).
- If a user-triggered tool call returns a binary attachment (PDF) and capture is enabled, we store an attachment stub: filename, mime-type, size, and a storage pointer. Redirects to object storage are also governed by residency rules (region-specific buckets).
- When customers enable long-term archival for compliance, we create a dedicated archival partition; those records are kept per the customer's contract (e.g., 7 years) and are outside the default 30-day bucket.

Data residency and opt-outs:
- Default residency follows the customer's selected region (us/eu/apac). Customers may request erasure of specific records via the console or API; erasure triggers tombstone + purge workflow described above. For EU customers with data erasure requests we follow the same purge timeline but ensure deletion occurs within the EU-resident storage.

SOC2-ready artifacts we can provide:
- Retention matrix (attached)
- A one-page statement we can sign-off on for BrightBank
- Audit logs showing purge job runs (for recent windows) — may require an NDA scope if we include identifiers

Attachment: retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (contains table mapping item -> default retention -> opt-out path -> related config flag).

Links: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/data-retention-overview

If that covers it, we can follow up with a short, signed statement you can include in evidence.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
